configs.name: Generated: dealereprocess

notes_for_human_review: Platform identified as DealerEProcess (dealereprocess.com / dep). The class 'dealereprocess' is inferred from CDN URLs (cdn.dealereprocess.org, dealereprocess.com) and script patterns.

year/make/model/trim are all parsed from the single .vehicle_title a element — the client must parse the full title string (e.g. 'Used 2016 Kia Sorento EX'). No individual selectors exist for each field.

price on the card: The dealer uses 'Jack Says Yes Price' / 'Jack Says Yes $pecial' as their final advertised price label (includes Documentation Fee of $799). The selector .details_master_price_display__price span targets that final price in the Details tab of the card. Confirm this is the correct total-fee-inclusive price.
VIN on the card is not in a standard element — it is available as the data-vin attribute on the root div.vehicle_item. The client should read: document.querySelector('.vehicle_item').dataset.vin.

mileage on the card is in .single-line-details__item — the second item contains 'Mileage XXXXX' text. For new inventory cards this element may not be present. The client will need to strip the 'Mileage ' label prefix.

Detail page: exterior_color, interior_color, mileage, VIN selectors use nth-child positional selectors inside .tabbable_container__content--showing. These are fragile if the order of detail_node items changes between vehicles. The human hint says to click the 'Details' tab first; the scraper must click tabbable_container__header:nth-child(2) or the tab labeled 'Details' before reading attributes.

Detail page sale_price: The final price label varies — 'Jack Says Yes Price' for used, 'Jack Says Yes $pecial' for new. Both use the same .details_master_price_display__price span selector so this should be stable, but confirm across more vehicles.

processing_fee / doc fee: The $799 Documentation Fee is shown as a separate line in the pricing breakdown and appears to be INCLUDED in the final 'Jack Says Yes Price'. Confirm this with the dealer — if the final price already includes the doc fee, the current sale_price selector is correct.
retail_price: For used vehicles, 'Retail Price' is shown separately. For new vehicles, 'MSRP' is shown. Neither is targeted since we only want the final advertised price.
sold_indicators: These are inferred/guessed. Manual verification of what actually appears in the HTML/JS when a vehicle is sold or removed is strongly recommended.

Photo URLs are in both src and data-src. The src attribute is set to a loading GIF for lazy-loaded images; data-src contains the real URL. The scraper should prefer data-src over src for gallery images.
body_style is not available as a dedicated element in the Details tab (only Doors count is shown). Set to null; client may derive from vehicle title or JSON-LD @type if needed.
The new inventory card for the Jetta does not show mileage in .single-line-details (new car). Selectors should handle absent mileage gracefully.
